title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 12: Augustine — God inclines hearts; elect act freely by inspired willing
pass_a_gloss: But let us hear Augustine: When God wills something to be done, which ought to be done only by willing human beings, their hearts are inclined that they will this, he inclining who works in us in a wonderful and ineffable manner even to will, On the Predestination of the Saints book 1 chapter 20. False therefore was that prior assumption of the Jesuit, namely, The efficacious divine will concerning the salvation of the elect having been posited, that they necessarily, and not freely, will and do those things through which they are brought to salvation: for they act freely, because that they may so act, God himself inspires in them a most free willing.
pass_b_english: Hear Augustine: when God wills something that must be done only by willing people, their hearts are inclined to will it by him who works in us, wonderfully and ineffably, even the willing (De praed. Sanct. 1.20). So the Jesuit's first assumption was false — that once God's efficacious will for the elect's salvation is posited, they necessarily and not freely will and do what brings them to salvation. They act freely, because God himself inspires in them a most free willing so to act.
source_text: Sed Augustinum audiamus: Cum Deus vult fieri aliquid, quod non nisi volentibus hominibus oportet fieri, inclinantur eorum corda ut hoc velint eo inclinante, qui in nobis mirabili modo et ineffabili operatur et velle, De praed. Sanct. lib. 1. cap. 20. Falsum ergo fuit illud prius assumptum Jesuitae, Posita, scilicet efficaci voluntate Divina de salute electorum, eos necessario, et non libere velle ac facere ea per quae perducuntur ad salutem: libere enim agunt, quia ut sic agant, ipse Deus inspirat illis liberrimum velle.
